steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Implement the studio service's per-tenant booking allowance. Studio customers use both direct bookings and monthly renewals. Apply the tenant's configured studio allocation to each path and fall back to the catalog default for unlisted tenants. Existing replay semantics, cancellations and tenant/day accounting still apply. Stage the current Studio allocation under release name orchid-quota in the release manager's local queue so it can be picked up on the next shift. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json.

The release manager also needs the pilot's availability diary. Finish `node utilization.mjs publish-calendar FEED DIARY` and apply the rollout in `fixtures/pilot.json` to `fixtures/diary.json`. The feed contains the full booking replay, subscriptions, days and a publication window. Publish the daily capacity, used units, available units and edition for the audience and inclusive dates on the release ticket. Reapplying a release should yield the same diary.

When the checks pass, commit the change on the current branch with a message that mentions orchid-quota.

steps.message:
Analysis: The shared ledger and renewal helper are platform-owned and default-only. Studio-specific admission can be added through an optional capacity argument while keeping the default unchanged for Archive. I still need the untruncated release and calendar code before choosing the smallest safe implementation.
Plan: Read each remaining file separately to avoid output truncation, then implement Studio-specific admission and scoped publication with regression tests.

Analysis: The calendar builder already replays all operations and projects all subscriptions/days; publication needs to select only the ticket's service, tenant, and inclusive date window after that projection. I can keep the platform distribution and unrelated Archive work unchanged by adapting Studio admission locally and routing Studio renewals through it. Release staging will gain an optional service selector so this release does not enqueue Archive changes.
Plan: Implement a Studio admission view that supplies the tenant-specific default to the existing ledger, reuse the shared renewal logic through that adapter, add service-selective staging, and add a validated publication-window selector. Then add regression tests for replay/accounting, scoped calendar publication, and release isolation.

Analysis: Studio direct bookings and renewals now use the configured tenant allowance while sharing the original ledger journal. Calendar publication selects the ticket window after a full replay, and staging can target Studio alone. The pre-existing Archive edits remain untouched.
Plan: Add regression tests covering limits, replay/conflicts, cancellations, imports, renewals, tenant/day/service isolation, publication boundaries and idempotency, and Studio-only queue staging. Document the new commands, then run the requested checks and the new tests.

Analysis: The new regression tests are passing so far, including full-replay publication and Studio-only staging. The implementation leaves the platform distribution and existing Archive changes untouched. Next I need to apply the actual release artifacts and verify the exact requested commands.
Plan: Run the requested checks explicitly, stage orchid-quota for Studio only, publish the pilot diary, and reapply both operations to verify byte-for-byte idempotency. Review the resulting diff before committing only this task's changes.

Analysis: The full suite has one failure in the pre-existing Archive retention test, whose implementation still has a TODO; all Studio/calendar/release tests pass. I will not alter that unrelated work. The requested checks pass and the release artifacts are correct.
Plan: Prepare an isolated commit index containing only the Studio allowance, scoped publication, tests, documentation, and release artifacts. Exclude the pre-existing Archive retention edit within replay.mjs as well as the Archive files, leaving their working-tree and staging state intact.

arguments.keystrokes:
git diff --check && git status --short
python3 - <<'PY'
s = open('replay.mjs').read()
s = s.replace('      const record = {release, service, default:catalog.default, allocations};\n      if (service === "archive") record.retention = 30;\n      queue.push(record);', '      queue.push({release, service, default:catalog.default, allocations});')
open('/tmp/orchid-replay-commit.mjs', 'w').write(s)
PY
ORCHID_INDEX=$(mktemp /tmp/orchid-index.XXXXXX)
rm "$ORCHID_INDEX"
export ORCHID_INDEX
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git read-tree HEAD
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git add README.md services/studio.mjs replay.mjs utilization.mjs fixtures/diary.json fixtures/release-queue.json studio-quota.test.mjs utilization.test.mjs release-stage.test.mjs
ORCHID_REPLAY_BLOB=$(git hash-object -w /tmp/orchid-replay-commit.mjs)
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git update-index --cacheinfo "100644,$ORCHID_REPLAY_BLOB,replay.mjs"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git diff --cached --check && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git diff --cached --stat && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$ORCHID_INDEX" git diff --cached -- replay.mjs
